 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.06.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.974/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, & CJM, MACT, MANDYA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF Rs.2,55,500/- WITH INTEREST @ 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL DEPOSIT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.974/2015 dated 05.06.2017 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM and MACT, at Mandya.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.

2. It is the case of the claimant that on 23.05.2015, the claimant by holding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-11/EC-1629 at around 10 a.m., was standing on the left side of the road, at that time, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-11/V-6948 came in a rash and NC: 2023:KHC:41473 negligent manner and dashed against the claimant, due to which he fell down and sustained injuries.
He has suffered lacerated wounds of the left foot, tenderness over toe and another lacerated wound on the part of the web space of left foot.
He was admitted in the hospital for nearly more than one and a half months as inpatient and spent huge amount for the treatment.

It is the case of the claimant that he was a pigmy collector, also agriculturist and was earning an amount of Rs.15,000/-
per month and because of the injuries sustained by him, he is unable to work.

3. It is the case of the Insurance Company that though in the FIR, statement of witnesses and the final report, they have mentioned the registration number of the vehicle as KA-11/U-6948 and the charge sheet is also filed on that number.
But, in the claim petition, it is mentioned as KA-11/V-6948.
It is submitted that though the accident had occurred on 23.05.2015, the complaint was given on 13.06.2015 there is a considerable delay.
It is submitted that the circumstances clearly shows that the NC: 2023:KHC:41473 involvement of the vehicle is not there and it has been implicated for the purpose of claiming compensation.

He submits that all the injuries sustained by him are simple in nature, but the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings and towards loss of earning, for 10 months, considering the income at Rs.7,500/- an amount of Rs.75,000/- was granted.
He submits that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was without any basis and is on the higher side.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal by rightly considering the injuries had granted compensation.
He had drawn the attention of the Court to the photographs which show the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant.
He submits that as there is a crush injury, it would take a lot of time for him to get back to work and the Court below had rightly granted the compensation for 10 months.

It is submitted that when he has examined the Investigating NC: 2023:KHC:41473 officer, he had categorically mentioned that because of the typographical mistake instead of mentioning the alphabet 'V', they have mentioned alphabet 'U'.

In fact, the charge sheet is filed against the owner of the vehicle as mentioned in the claim petition but not against the owner of the vehicle as mentioned in the FIR and charge sheet, and it is a typographical mistake.
He further submits that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is reasonable.
5. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
The first and foremost issue that is urged before this Court is about the involvement of the vehicle.

As far as the involvement and mentioning of the registration number of the vehicle is concerned, the Investigation Officer has deposed that due to typographical mistake, instead of mentioning KA-11/V-6948, they have mentioned the registration number as KA-11/U-6948 and they have filed the charge sheet against the owner of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- NC: 2023:KHC:41473 11/V-6948.
It strengthens the case of the claimant that it is a typographical mistake.
Secondly, the delay in giving the complaint has to be considered basing on the facts of each and every case.
In this case it is stated that as the owner has assured to settle the claim he has not given the complaint also assumes relevance.
In these facts and circumstances and this Court do not find any force in the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant.
6. Then coming to the aspect of compensation, though it is stated that they are simple injuries, this Court has perused the injuries sustained by the claimant.
Looking at those injuries, the Court below had rightly granted compensation under the head of pain and suffering and medical expenses are not disputed.
Coming to the attendant charges, nourishment and the loss of amenities only an amount of Rs.10,000/- each was granted.
But, when it comes to the loss of income, during the laid up period granting loss of income for 10 NC: 2023:KHC:41473 months is on the higher side.
This Court is inclined to grant only of 5 months, which comes to 5x7,500 = Rs.37,500/-.

The claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.2,17,500/-.
7.

The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Compensation  Awarded 1. Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 50,000/-
2.

Medical expenses : Rs. 1,10,500/-
 Transport, nourishment and 3. : Rs. 10,000/-
 attendant charges 4. Loss of amenities : Rs. 10,000/-
5. Loss of income : Rs. 37,500/-
